back2basics.text: Commercial coal mining auctions are a process where the government offers coal blocks to private companies through competitive bidding. This system allows multiple players to participate, encouraging investment and efficient resource use. The auctions are designed to ensure transparency and attract new investors by allowing 100% foreign direct investment and no restrictions on coal end-use.

2026-11-21-am-082ef47973.deck: The Ministry of Coal conducted the 16th round of commercial coal mine auctions, receiving 85 bids for 18 coal blocks, including 20 first-time bidders. This strong response highlights coal's continuing role in India's energy security and economic growth, relevant for understanding resource management and energy policies in UPSC exams.

back2basics.concept: Foreign Exchange Management Act (FEMA) and Authorised Dealers
back2basics.text: FEMA regulates foreign exchange transactions in India to facilitate external trade and payments. Authorised Dealers are banks or entities authorised by the RBI to deal in foreign exchange and provide services to exporters and importers, ensuring compliance with FEMA rules.

back2basics.concept: Core Sector and Its Economic Significance
back2basics.text: The core sector comprises key industries such as coal, crude oil, natural gas, refinery products, steel, cement, electricity, and fertilizers that are fundamental to the economy's infrastructure and industrial activity. Growth in these sectors is a leading indicator of economic health because they supply essential inputs to other industries. The Index of Core Industries measures monthly production changes in these sectors to track industrial momentum and infrastructure development.

back2basics.text: Treasury Bills (T-Bills) are short-term debt instruments issued by the government to meet short-term funding needs. They are issued at a discount and redeemed at face value on maturity, with tenures typically ranging from a few weeks to one year. T-Bills are considered safe investments and are used by the central bank to manage liquidity in the economy.

back2basics.concept: Know Your Customer (KYC) and Internal Ombudsman
back2basics.text: KYC is a process by which financial institutions verify the identity and address of their customers to prevent fraud and money laundering. back2basics.concept: State Government Securities and Debt Management
back2basics.text: State Government Securities (SGS) are debt instruments issued by state governments to finance their fiscal deficits. Debt management involves managing the timing and cost of repayments to ensure fiscal sustainability. Conversion or switch auctions allow states to exchange existing securities for new ones with different maturities, helping them manage liquidity and rollover risks effectively.

2026-11-21-am-cbaf2a868f.deck: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has announced an auction for the conversion or switch of State Government Securities (SGS) aggregating ₹10,800 crore face value. This process affects state finances and debt management, which is important for understanding fiscal federalism in India.

body.label: Definition
body.text: Conversion or switch is a process where state governments exchange existing securities (source securities) for new securities (destination securities) with different maturities through an auction.

body.label: Purpose
body.text: It helps states manage their debt by altering the maturity profile of their liabilities without changing the overall amount significantly.

sections.heading: What is the conversion/switch of State Government Securities?

body.label: Auction details
body.text: The auction is multiple-price based, where bids specify the amount and price of source and destination securities, and successful bids are accepted at their quoted prices.

body.label: Bidding process
body.text: Market participants submit bids electronically on RBI's e-Kuber platform, specifying the face value of source securities they want to sell and the price for destination securities they want to buy.

body.label: Settlement
body.text: The auction settlement happens on T+1 basis, with fund settlement covering net accrued interest and any cash consideration due to rounding-off.

sections.heading: How does the RBI conduct the conversion/switch auction?

body.label: Aggregate amount
body.text: The auction covers an aggregate face value of ₹10,800 crore across Madhya Pradesh, Punjab, Rajasthan, Tamil Nadu, and Uttar Pradesh.

body.label: Source and destination securities
body.text: Source securities are mostly shorter-term SDLs maturing between 2027 and 2029, switched to longer-term SGS maturing between 2034 and 2044.

sections.heading: Which State Government Securities are involved in the current auction?

body.label: Debt management tool
body.text: Conversion/switch auctions allow states to manage their debt maturity profiles, improving fiscal sustainability and reducing rollover risks.

body.label: Impact on state finances
body.text: By extending maturities, states can ease short-term repayment pressures, which is crucial for maintaining fiscal discipline under the federal structure.

back2basics.concept: Panchayati Raj Institutions and Fiscal Decentralisation
back2basics.text: Panchayati Raj Institutions (PRIs) are rural local self-government bodies responsible for planning and implementing development programs at the village level. Fiscal decentralisation refers to the process of transferring financial powers and resources from central and state governments to local bodies like PRIs, enabling them to raise revenues and manage expenditures to meet local needs effectively.

2026-11-21-am-efc5ecdcc7.deck: The Reserve Bank of India released its second biennial report assessing the finances of Gram Panchayats from 2022-23 to 2024-25, focusing on their fiscal health and role in rural development. This is important for UPSC aspirants to understand rural governance, fiscal decentralisation, and challenges in local self-government financing.

editor.why: Critical for understanding decentralisation, rural governance and fiscal devolution.

body.label: Report scope
body.text: The report analyses a balanced panel of 2.25 lakh Gram Panchayats covering 2022-23 to 2024-25, focusing on their finances and role in rural socio-economic development.

body.label: Revenue sources
body.text: Gram Panchayats depend on intergovernmental transfers for about 90% of their receipts, while own source revenues constitute only about 10%, mainly from non-tax sources like interest receipts, programme funds, and user charges.

body.label: Expenditure priorities
body.text: Expenditure is largely aligned with the Fifteenth Finance Commission mandates and national schemes, with water supply and sanitation accounting for about 40% of total spending.

body.label: Progress and disparities
body.text: There has been progress in rural connectivity, electrification, water supply, sanitation, and community assets, but inter-State disparities in access, quality, and functionality persist.

body.label: Challenges ahead
body.text: As some large Gram Panchayats transition to Town Panchayats, their functional responsibilities may outpace fiscal and administrative readiness, requiring fiscal support, capacity building, and improved own revenue collection through better property tax and license fee rationalisation.

sections.heading: What does the RBI report on Panchayati Raj finances reveal?

body.label: Decentralisation insight
body.text: The report provides empirical data on fiscal decentralisation and the financial autonomy of rural local bodies, a key topic in governance and federalism.

body.label: Rural governance challenges
body.text: Understanding the dependence on transfers and limited own revenues highlights challenges in empowering Panchayati Raj Institutions for sustainable rural development.

body.label: Fiscal policy relevance
body.text: The report links local government finances with national fiscal policies like the Fifteenth Finance Commission, relevant for questions on fiscal federalism and budgeting.
